profile.headline: Adjunct Professor at Columbus State University & Principle Software Engineer at Pratt & Whitney
profile.summary:
I work at the intersection of technology, data, business, and education.
Professionally, I serve as a Principal Software Engineer in aerospace manufacturing, where my work focuses on software solutions, manufacturing systems, data, process improvement, and digital transformation. My background spans technology, analytics, business intelligence, operations, quality, and leadership, giving me a broad perspective on how technology can solve real business problems.

I also serve as an Adjunct Professor at Columbus State University, teaching undergraduate courses in information systems and business technology. My industry experience comes into the classroom with me—I want students to understand not only the concepts behind information systems, but how technology is actually used to make decisions, improve processes, solve problems, and support organizations.

As a Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, continuous improvement is also a significant part of how I approach both technology and business. I’m particularly interested in the relationship between systems, data, processes, and the people who depend on them.

My work and teaching currently center around:
• Software Engineering & Manufacturing Applications
• Information Systems
• Data & Business Intelligence
• Digital Transformation
• Process Improvement & Operational Excellence
• Lean Six Sigma
• Technology & Business Strategy
• Higher Education

I enjoy the opportunity to work on both sides of the industry–academia connection: building and improving technology in practice while helping prepare students to use it in their own careers.

positions.title: Adjunct Professor
positions.description:
Teach undergraduate courses in information systems and business technology, connecting foundational concepts with real-world applications in technology, data, analytics, and digital transformation. Develop and deliver course content, hands-on activities, assessments, and applied learning experiences designed to strengthen students' technical and business problem-solving skills.

Courses:
• MISM 3115 – Principles of Information Systems Management
• BUSA 2100 – Introduction to Information Systems in Business

positions.title: Customer Care Analyst
positions.description: Resolved customer inquiries regarding insurance benefits and claims through empathetic communication. Conducted research and analysis to identify root causes of issues, improving customer service processes. Documented inquiry outcomes to ensure accurate tracking and continuous improvement.
positions.insights: Skills: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) · Analytical Skills · Presentation Skills · Problem Solving

positions.title: Commercial Division Manager
positions.description: Managed a $600M budget and led a team of 10, streamlining property appraisal processes to enhance operational efficiency. Developed and implemented standard procedures, provided technical support for appraisal software systems, and conducted detailed workflow analysis. Identified areas for revaluation, supervised fieldwork, and made strategic recommendations for process improvements. Created and maintained coding for appraisal software, ensuring accurate property valuations. Collaborated with stakeholders to document current processes and supported business case creation
